campaigns.context: Hundreds of subdomains across 11 numerically-patterned apex domains (014901490149h/x/y/z/f/i/j/w.com and www01490258/43/60dd.com) embed a baidu label plus a date token in each subdomain name, consistent with Baidu brand impersonation or search-engine abuse. All apex domains were reported by a single researcher on August 4 with over 270 combined IOCs. The shared numeric-suffix naming pattern indicates coordinated infrastructure provisioning by a single actor.
campaigns.name: Baidu phishing wave on 014901490149* family domains

campaigns.context: Subdomains on catex.at and locaz.icu serve phishing pages at the path /cnbcard/web_sms_activate.php, consistent with a fake card activation flow that harvests SMS one-time passwords. The shared path structure across two unrelated apex domains indicates a common phishing kit deployed on multiple hosts. One researcher reported 19 IOCs on August 4.
campaigns.name: Bank card SMS activation phishing on catex.at and locaz.icu

campaigns.context: Multiple domains impersonate Telegram using deliberate misspellings - telergam-cdn* subdomains on aa9977rt.com, telegramtghg.com.cn, and fi-telegram.hl.cn - to host phishing pages targeting Telegram users. The Chinese ccTLD usage and .cn-registered subdomains suggest a focus on Chinese-speaking users. A single researcher reported all three clusters on August 4.
campaigns.name: Telegram impersonation phishing on typosquat domains

campaigns.context: Twelve IP addresses tagged as Evilginx adversary-in-the-middle phishing infrastructure were reported by Team Cymru S2 on August 6. Evilginx proxies legitimate login pages to intercept credentials and session cookies, bypassing multi-factor authentication. The IPs span multiple hosting providers and geographic regions, indicating distributed phishing campaign infrastructure.
campaigns.name: Evilginx adversary-in-the-middle phishing IP cluster

campaigns.context: Four .cfd domains - vokser.cfd, rdwksm.cfd, vorlen.cfd, and qbnzgt.cfd - serve phishing redirect pages where Cloudflare IP addresses are embedded directly in the URL path after a short token, for example /Ek41lT172.67.157.36CAPTCHA. The CAPTCHA suffix in some paths suggests a fake human-verification lure. Multiple researchers reported combined IOCs on August 3.
campaigns.name: Phishing on .cfd domains with IP embedded in URL path

campaigns.context: Sliver C2 framework is distributed via multiple GitHub repositories using lookalike organization names such as business-N and bytecategory, with a Cloudflare Worker at package-proxy.cf19-427.workers.dev providing proxy routing. The C2 infrastructure resolves to 43.157.204.73 with c2.ashveil.org as a callback domain. Five researchers reported 15 IOCs between July 31 and August 3.
campaigns.name: Sliver C2 distributed via GitHub lookalike repositories

campaigns.context: Nine Android malware samples linked to a Pastebin raw URL (pastebin.com/raw/uh8JXav2) are tagged as Android Trojan. The distinct MD5 hashes suggest active repackaging or multiple payload variants staged at the same URL. Three researchers reported 10 IOCs between August 4 and 6.
campaigns.name: Android Trojan distributed via Pastebin staging URL

campaigns.context: Eight IP addresses - a near-consecutive block of 188.127.246.70 through 188.127.246.76 plus 151.243.113.23 - are tagged as Magecart payment-card skimmer infrastructure. The tight sequential IP range suggests a single hosting customer provisioning dedicated skimmer back-end capacity. One researcher from Team Cymru S2 reported 8 IOCs on August 4.
campaigns.name: Magecart skimmer C2 IP cluster

campaigns.context: Phishing pages at /login paths on dslkk.cn, niuaniu.top, and raaglpfplzp.top target Japanese bank customers, consistent with Resona Bank impersonation previously identified for this cluster. The uniform /login path across geographically diverse hosts is consistent with a shared phishing kit. Two researchers reported 6 IOCs between August 5 and 7.
campaigns.name: Resona Bank phishing via /login pages

campaigns.context: Three randomized subdomains on edgeone.dev, Tencent's edge cloud platform, are tagged as phishing pages and were active from August 2 to 7. Hosting phishing on legitimate cloud infrastructure reduces the effectiveness of domain-based blocking. One reporter flagged 6 IOCs with no identified targeted brand.
campaigns.name: Phishing hosted on Tencent EdgeOne cloud platform

campaigns.context: Open directories on nfe.boletos-notas.com, pdf-bro.lat, and dnf.nfexmlfiscal.com.br serve Brazilian Nota Fiscal Eletronica invoice-themed ZIP archives with names such as Nota_-SZESAW.zip, consistent with malware delivery via fake invoice lures. The uniform nfe subdomain pattern and stage-N tracking paths across multiple domains suggest a shared deployment kit. Three reporters flagged 15 IOCs between July 31 and August 5.
campaigns.name: Brazilian NF-e invoice lure via open directory

campaigns.context: Compromised shared hosting accounts at apreciaciones.com, baddiehub.com.co, and aunquenolocreas.com host phishing pages under a /~netcentrixco/intesasanpaolo/ path, impersonating the Italian bank Intesa Sanpaolo. The netcentrixco component suggests a recurring actor using the same directory structure across multiple breached hosts. One researcher reported 6 IOCs between August 1 and 2.
campaigns.name: Intesa Sanpaolo phishing on shared hosting

campaigns.context: Randomized domains mu-hiqwnkesad.com and mg-euwqnasnd.com serve phishing pages using a /pc_NNNN/sp_NNNuNNN/login/loginUsername path structure consistent with Japanese banking credential harvesting. The numeric codes in the path may encode victim or session identifiers. Two researchers reported 6 IOCs between August 1 and 5.
campaigns.name: Japanese bank login phishing on randomized domains

campaigns.context: Phishing pages under the path /jmFfvPRN/ appear on urbanizab2b.com, a Spanish B2B platform, and vignobles-lorgeril.com, a French winery, both likely compromised legitimate hosts. An /ip endpoint variant suggests victim IP geolocation or filtering is in use to serve targeted content. Two researchers reported 5 IOCs on August 5.
campaigns.name: Phishing kit on compromised legitimate sites via /jmFfvPRN/ path

campaigns.context: Subdomains a2 and e1 on cdnresolver.com are tagged as stealer command-and-control endpoints. The domain name mimics a legitimate CDN resolver service to blend malicious traffic with routine network infrastructure lookups. One researcher reported 4 IOCs on August 4.
campaigns.name: Stealer C2 infrastructure on cdnresolver.com

campaigns.context: Eliice.com, a scam site previously observed alongside the lookalike domain eliece.vip, continues to be flagged with 4 IOCs. The same two researchers flagged both domains on August 1-2, suggesting a single actor operating near-identical sites under slightly different names to capture mistyped traffic.
campaigns.name: Scam cluster on eliice.com and eliece.vip
